title: The Red Kite
description: Nia and Teo learn that losing something doesn't always mean losing it forever.

cover.alt: Nia and Teo hold their red kite beneath a big oak tree.

illustration.alt: Nia and Teo in the schoolyard with their red kite after the rain.

blocks.title: The Red Kite
lines: The rain stopped just after lunch. Nia looked across the schoolyard. There was a patch of blue in the sky.
“Now we can try!” she told Teo.
They had waited all week to fly their red kite. Nia took the spool while Teo watched closely. A breeze lifted the kite a little. They both jumped with joy.

variants.prompt: What had Nia and Teo been waiting all week to do?

options.text: Fly their red kite
Go to school
Watch the rain

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! They had waited to fly their red kite.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for what Nia and Teo had been waiting to do.

variants.prompt: What sign told them they could finally fly the kite?

options.text: A patch of blue appeared in the sky after the rain
Teo asked the teacher
The spool came undone by itself

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! The sky cleared just after lunch.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about what Nia sees in the sky at the start.

illustration.alt: The red kite gets caught on a high branch of an oak tree.

blocks.title: Caught in the Oak
lines: Then a strong gust came. The string slipped from Nia’s fingers. The kite rose, spun once, and landed in the big oak. Its blue tail caught on a high branch.
“It’s gone,” Teo whispered.
Nia looked up. They could still see red among the leaves, but the branch was much too high.

variants.prompt: What made the kite land in the oak?

options.text: A strong gust of wind came
Nia let go on purpose
Teo threw it too high

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! A strong gust came and the string slipped from Nia's fingers.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for what happened right before the kite rose.

variants.prompt: Why could Nia and Teo still see the kite but not get it back?

options.text: The branch where it was caught was too high to reach
The kite had completely broken apart
They didn't know which tree it fell in

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! They could see red among the leaves, but the branch was out of reach.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about what Nia says about the branch at the end of the page.

illustration.alt: Nia and Teo ask the schoolyard caretaker for help getting the kite back.

blocks.title: Asking for Help
lines: Teo stepped toward the trunk.
“We aren’t going to climb,” Nia said. “That branch is too high.”
They sat under the tree for a moment. Teo’s eyes filled with tears. Nia felt sad too, but she saw the school caretaker passing by.
“Let’s ask him for help,” she said.
Nia explained where the blue tail was. He looked in the direction Nia pointed.

variants.prompt: Why did Nia decide to ask for help instead of climbing the tree?

options.text: Because the branch was too high to climb safely
Because she didn't care about the kite
Because Teo forbade it

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! She said they weren't going to climb because the branch was too high.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for Nia's exact words about the branch.

variants.prompt: What helped Nia ask for help clearly?

options.text: Knowing exactly where the blue tail was so she could point it out
Teo stopping his crying first
The teacher calling them over

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! Nia explained where the blue tail was so the caretaker knew where to look.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about what Nia does right after asking for help.

illustration.alt: The caretaker uses a long pole to bring the kite down from the tree.

blocks.title: The Long Pole
lines: The caretaker brought a long pole. Nia and Teo waited several steps from the tree.
The tip touched the kite. The kite moved once. Then again. At last it came free and floated down to the ground.
“It’s back!” Teo cried.
Nia thanked the caretaker. When she picked up the kite, she noticed a small tear near the center.

variants.prompt: What did the caretaker use to bring the kite down?

options.text: A long pole
A ladder
A new string

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! He brought a long pole.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for what the caretaker brings.

variants.prompt: What did Nia discover right when she got the kite back?

options.text: A small tear near the center
That the blue tail was gone
That the spool was broken

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! She noticed a small tear near the center when she picked it up.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the last sentence of the page.

illustration.alt: Nia and Teo patch the kite at a courtyard table.

blocks.title: The Patch
lines: “It can’t fly like that,” Teo said.
“Not yet,” Nia answered.
At a courtyard table, they laid the kite face up. The caretaker gave them a bit of strong paper and tape. Nia held the kite. Teo smoothed the patch with care.
The patch felt firm. Nia gave the blue tail a very gentle tug to check that it was still tied on.

variants.prompt: What did Nia and Teo do before flying the kite again?

options.text: They patched the tear
They bought a new kite
They asked the teacher to fix it

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! They put a patch of strong paper over the tear.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for what Nia and Teo do at the courtyard table.

variants.prompt: Why did Nia gently tug the blue tail before trying to fly the kite?

options.text: To check it was still tied on well, not just that the patch was firm
Because she wanted to remove the tail
Because Teo asked her to, as a game

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! She wanted to make sure everything — the patch and the tail — was ready.
variants.retryFeedback: Reread the last sentence of the page.

illustration.alt: The patched red kite flies high over the oak tree in the sunshine.

blocks.title: Higher Than Before
lines: Later, the breeze returned. Nia took the string, and Teo held the kite until the air lifted it. This time Nia held the spool firmly.
The red kite flew above the oak. Its little patch shone in the sun.
“It looks like a star,” Teo said.
Nia smiled. They had lost the kite for a while, but they found a way to bring it back. Now it flew higher than before.

variants.prompt: What did Nia do differently with the spool this time?

options.text: She held it firmly
She gave it to Teo
She left it on the ground

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! This time Nia held the spool firmly.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for what Nia does with the spool at the start of the page.

variants.prompt: What did Nia and Teo learn by the end of the story?

options.text: That losing something doesn't always mean it's lost for good
That you should never fly kites near trees
That the caretaker doesn't like to help

variants.correctFeedback: That's it! They found a way to bring it back, and it flew higher than before.
variants.retryFeedback: Think about what Nia says at the end about losing the kite.

gust.example: A gust of wind blew my grandfather's hat right off his head.

caught.definition: Stuck and not easy to free.
caught.example: The ball got caught in the branches of the tree.

tear.example: He fixed the tear in his backpack with a little glue.

patch.definition: A small piece that covers a tear.
patch.example: She sewed a patch onto the knee of her jeans.

spool.definition: An object that string is wound around.
spool.example: He wound the fishing line onto a plastic spool.

caretaker.definition: A person who takes care of a place, like a school.
caretaker.example: The caretaker unlocked the gym early for the morning game.

schoolyard.definition: The outdoor area of a school where children play.
schoolyard.example: We play tag in the schoolyard every recess.

several.definition: More than two or three, but not a lot.
several.example: She invited several friends to her birthday party.
